newsitem.title: UK: Euro shares firm as markets await Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Euro shares firm as markets await Fed meeting.

text.p: European stock markets rose on Tuesday, but most investors sat firmly on the fence before the U.S. Federal Reserve met to discuss the issue which has haunted this year's bull runs -- interest rates.
The dollar was quietly mixed but again dealers were mesmerised by a two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FMOC) starting on Tuesday.

With the United States apparently enjoying inflation-free economic growth, logic dictates that the FMOC -- the Fed's policy-making arm -- should leave rates unchanged. But no announcement was expected before the end of the meeting on Wednesday.
Tuesday was the third anniversary of a U.S. interest rate hike which caught investors off guard and sent share prices tumbling globally.
This time nobody is taking any chances, particularly in London where British monetary authorities are also meeting on Wednesday.

"Recent figures show there's really no threat of inflation heating up, so there's no reason to raise rates," said one London share dealer. "But I would have thought the market needs to get these meetings out of the way." he said.
By mid-morning the main European bourses were all up despite a small FMOC-inspired drop on Wall Street overnight.

London's FTSE-100 index was up 13.8 points at 4,271.6 while Frankfurt's DAX, which closed at a record on Monday, rose 11.77 to 3,074.06. Paris was likewise firmer with the CAC-40 4.02 points higher at 2,512.57.
But everywhere caution was the watchword, reflected in the Dow Jones industrial average which closed down 6.93 points at 6,806.16 on Monday.
That included the foreign exchange markets, where the dollar flirted with 1.64 marks in quiet trade.

"With the FOMC meeting, I don't think anyone's going to want to do very much, so I think we're in for a fairly range-bound day until we get something out of the FOMC," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
The dollar was at 1.6405 marks and 122.20 yen at midmorning, down from its late Monday European level of 1.6436 marks but up from 121.83 yen.
The dollar may no longer be hitting highs but the tone remains firm before a meeting this weekend of finance ministers of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in Berlin.
"The strength of the dollar is being underpinned by comments by Japanese officials playing down prospects of concerted intervention coming out of the G7 meeting," said Adam Chester,
